key_insight: Indoor photovoltaics paired with (anti)ferroelectric energy storage and low-power computing could enable autonomous edge AI nodes that reduce reliance on centralized data centres.
engineering_relevance: Reliable distributed intelligence requires co-designing indoor energy harvesting, storage and computation to match local power availability with device demand.
method: Assess indoor photovoltaic requirements for distributed intelligence.
Discuss how emerging photovoltaic materials meet these requirements and address remaining gaps.
Examine (anti)ferroelectrics for electrostatic storage and low-power in-memory neuromorphic computing.
evidence_signal: The abstract presents a perspective on emerging technologies, not a demonstrated integrated system or quantified performance evaluation.
watch_item: Reliable operation remains contingent on matching variable indoor energy supply with storage capacity and computational workloads.
paper_title: Computing at the Edge Enabled by Indoor Photovoltaics and Ferroelectrics
